STARTERPhonics · Lesson 1
A–Z

The English Alphabet

English has 26 letters and about 40 sounds. This lesson shows how they work.

Introduction

126 letters

Aa Bb Cc Dd Ee Ff Gg Hh Ii Jj Kk Ll Mm Nn Oo Pp Qq Rr Ss Tt Uu Vv Ww Xx Yy Zz
Vowels (5): A  E  I  O  U Consonants (21): all the other letters

Y is a consonant, but sometimes it sounds like a vowel.  my · happy

2A letter has a name and a sound

We say the name when we spell a word. We say the sound when we read.

B Name/biː/ Sound/b/ As inbag
M Name/em/ Sound/m/ As inmap
S Name/es/ Sound/s/ As insun

3More sounds than letters

English has 26 letters but about 40 sounds. So one letter can have more than one sound, and two letters can work together to make one sound. You will learn them step by step.

4Sound symbols

A sound symbol shows how we say a sound, not how we write it. We write it between two lines.

/æ/the sound of A in cat
/iː/the mark ː means a long sound

5How to read this book

catOrange letters are the letters we are learning.
makeGrey letters are silent. We do not say them.
ALWAYSThe rule never changes.
USUALLY TRUEThe rule has a few exceptions.
NOT FIXED — LEARN EACH WORDThere is no rule. Learn each word.

Aa

The Letter A

A is the first letter of the alphabet. It is a vowel with four main sounds.

Vowel4 sounds

1The sounds of A

/æ/
Short A
  • cat
  • map
  • bag
/eɪ/
Long A — it says its name
  • baby
  • paper
  • radio
/ɑː/
Open A — open your mouth
  • want
  • wash
  • pasta
/ə/
Weak A — a soft, short sound
  • about
  • again
  • sofa

2When is A silent?

A is almost never silent on its own.

The Letter E

E is the most common letter in English. It has three main sounds.

Vowel3 sounds

  • even
/ə/
Weak E — a soft, short sound
  • open
  • problem

2When is E silent?

At the end of a word, E is usually silent.
It often helps the vowel before it say its name.

Grey letter = silent
USUALLY TRUE

Short words with only one vowel say the E:

STARTERSpeaking · Lesson 1

Hello! Nice to Meet You

Greetings and names

Say helloSay your nameAsk a name

1Read the conversation

It is the first day at Future Vision Institute. Adam meets Sara at the classroom door.
AADAMHi! I'm Adam.
SSARAHello, Adam. I'm Sara. Nice to meet you.
AADAMNice to meet you, too. Are you a new student?
SSARAYes, I am. It's my first day.
AADAMIt's my first day, too! Is this the Starter class?
SSARAYes, it is. Come in.
AADAMThanks, Sara.
SSARAYou're welcome.

2Useful phrases

Say hello

Hi! · Hello!
Good morning!

Say your name

I'm Adam.
My name is Adam.

Ask a name

What's your name?
— I'm Sara.

Meet someone

Nice to meet you.
— Nice to meet you, too.

Say thank you

Thanks. / Thank you.
— You're welcome.

Ask a question

Are you a new student?
— Yes, I am.

3New words

newfor the first time; not old
firstnumber one; before all the others
studenta person who learns at a school
classa group of students who learn together

Mr. Ali is writing the names of the new students.
MAMR. ALIGood morning. What's your full name, please?
AADAMMy name is Adam Hassan.
MAMR. ALIHow do you spell Hassan?
AADAMH - A - S - S - A - N.
MAMR. ALIThank you. Where are you from, Adam?
AADAMI'm from Sudan.
MAMR. ALIWhat's your phone number?
AADAMIt's 0912 345 678.
MAMR. ALIGreat. Welcome to the class, Adam!

2Useful phrases

Your full name

My name is Adam Hassan.

Spell a word

How do you spell that?
— H - A - S - S - A - N.

Where are you from?

Where are you from?
— I'm from Sudan.

Phone number

What's your phone number?
— It's 0912 345 678.

Be polite

please · thank you

Welcome someone

Welcome to the class!

3New words

full nameyour first name and your family name
spellsay the letters of a word, one by one
fromshows your home country or city
phone numberthe numbers you call to talk to someone

In the Classroom

Classroom language

Understand the teacherAsk for helpBe polite in class

1Read the conversation

Mr. Ali starts the lesson. Adam and Sara sit next to each other.
MAMR. ALIGood morning, everyone. Please open your books to page ten.
SSARAExcuse me, Mr. Ali. Can you repeat that, please?
MAMR. ALISure. Open your books to page ten.
AADAMMr. Ali, how do you say this word?
MAMR. ALILight. L - I - G - H - T. Listen and repeat: light.
AADAMLight. Sorry, I don't understand the G and H.
MAMR. ALINo problem. In IGH, the G and H are silent.
AADAMOh, I see. Thank you!
MAMR. ALIVery good. Now work in pairs.

2Useful phrases

The teacher says

Open your books.
Listen and repeat.

Work together

Work in pairs.

Ask again

Can you repeat that, please?

Ask about a word

How do you say this word?

Say you need help

Sorry, I don't understand.
— No problem.

Start politely

Excuse me, Mr. Ali.

3New words

pageone side of a sheet of paper in a book
repeatsay something again
pairsgroups of two people
excuse mea polite way to start talking to someone

My Family

Talking about your family

Talk about your familyAsk about brothers and sistersAsk how old someone is

1Read the conversation

After class, Adam and Sara drink tea in the institute café.
SSARADo you have brothers or sisters, Adam?
AADAMYes. I have two brothers and one sister.
SSARAThat's a big family!
AADAMYes, it is. And you?
SSARAI have one sister. Her name is Lina.
AADAMHow old is she?
SSARAShe's ten.
AADAMDo you live with your parents?
SSARAYes. I live with my mother, my father, and my sister.

2Useful phrases

Ask about family

Do you have brothers or sisters?
— Yes, I have two brothers.

Say no

Do you have a sister?
— No, I don't.

Give a name

Her name is Lina.
His name is Omar.

Ask about age

How old is she?
— She's ten.

Where you live

I live with my parents.

React

That's a big family!

3New words

brothera boy or man with the same parents as you
sistera girl or woman with the same parents as you
parentsyour mother and your father
familyparents, children, brothers and sisters

My Home

Talking about where you live

Say where you liveName the roomsUse there is and there are

1Read the conversation

Adam and Sara walk home from the institute.
AADAMWhere do you live, Sara?
SSARAI live in an apartment near the institute.
AADAMIs it big?
SSARANot very. There are two bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and a bathroom.
AADAMIs there a balcony?
SSARAYes, there is. I love it! Do you live in an apartment, too?
AADAMNo, I live in a house. There is a small garden.
SSARAThat's nice!

2Useful phrases

Ask where

Where do you live?
— I live in an apartment.

One thing

There is a kitchen.

Two or more

There are two bedrooms.

Ask if it is there

Is there a garden?
— Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.

Describe

It's big. · It's small.

React

That's nice!

3New words

apartmenta home on one floor of a big building

living rooma room where the family sits together
balconya small place outside an apartment, with a wall or rail
gardena place with grass, plants or trees next to a house
